accuracy_findings.claim: When the system is conquered, or you use Liberate or Abandon on it, its queue stays. Its orders keep building.
accuracy_findings.problem: True for building, upgrade and repair orders, but wrong for ship orders, which this page lists as queue items. Liberate, Abandon of a system and the conquest of a player system all run prepare_leaving_system. That removes the ship orders of the leaving player's Navarchs in the system from the queue, with no refund. The page also contradicts administrative-operations.md, which says Liberate and Abandon cancel the ship orders of your Navarchs there.
accuracy_findings.fix: Scope the sentence to buildings and add one sentence on ships, for example: "When the system is conquered, or you use Liberate or Abandon on it, its building, upgrade and repair orders stay and keep building. The ship orders of your Navarchs there are cancelled." Add player/agent.ex:1405-1426 and :1303-1308 to sources.
accuracy_findings.evidence: player/agent.ex:147 (Liberate), :198 (Abandon of a system) and :1027 (lose_system, cast by conquest.ex:150) call prepare_leaving_system (:1405-1426). For each of the owner's Navarchs in the system it calls clear_associated_production_queue (:1303-1308), which casts {:cancel_ordered_ships, id}. That becomes ProductionQueue.reject_items (stellar_system.ex:604-606, production_queue.ex:73-74). Run (tmp/help-review/construction-queue-acc-r0-hands.exs, Legacy, generated autonomous system) printed: queue before [{1, :building, :mine_dome, 1200}, {2, :ship, :fighter_1, 500}]. After claim by p1, claim by p2, claim as dominion and abandon, the queue was unchanged. After abandon, next_tick(1.0) gave [{1, :building, :mine_dome, 1160.0}, ...]. After cancel_ordered_ships(77) it was [{1, :building, :mine_dome, 1200}].

accuracy_findings.claim: Nothing is refunded to you, and you can no longer cancel them.
accuracy_findings.problem: A conquest's damage roll resolves before the system changes hands. If a hit tile had an upgrade in the queue, that upgrade is cancelled and its full credit goes to the defender. So the old owner can get credit back for queued upgrades in a conquest. The orders that remain in the queue are indeed never refunded.
accuracy_findings.fix: Narrow the wording, for example "Nothing still in the queue is refunded to you", or leave it as is, since the siege page owns upgrade hits.
accuracy_findings.evidence: conquest.ex:140-150: release_siege with damaged_buildings_count runs before lose_system and claim_system. stellar_system.ex:1734-1766: an upgrade hit is unqueued and refunded at level credit. stellar_system/agent.ex:237-245: the refund is cast to data.owner, the defender at that moment.

accuracy_findings.problem: The brief lists terms [construction queue, build queue, queue, cancel, refund]. 'build queue' is missing, so the glossary loses that entry. The alias build-queue is present.

The math is correct in both units: Legacy has 20 ticks per hour, so 100 per tick is 2000 per hour and 12 ticks is 0.6 hours. But the hour rendering mixes number formats in one line: "1,200 production ÷ 2000 production per hour = 0.6 hours". The rate token prints no thousands separator while the typed number has one.
accuracy_findings.fix: Either write the typed number without a separator (1200) so the line reads consistently, or ask the developer to give {rate:} output thousands separators.
accuracy_findings.evidence: --page output: 2000 production per hour ... 0.6 hours.

clarity_findings.claim: The closing sentence adds an unbriefed fact about ship orders that isn't authorized by this leaf's brief and reads as inconsistent with the sentence right before it.
clarity_findings.problem: Line 67 ends: "...its building, upgrade and repair orders stay and keep building. Nothing still in the queue is refunded to you, and you can no longer cancel those orders. The ship orders of your Navarchs there are cancelled, with no refund." The guide map's Q3 default for this page (guide-map.md "Q3" and §8.1 "Buildings verdicts") only says orders keep building, nothing is refunded, and cancelling is blocked — it says nothing about ship orders being treated differently. Guide-map §7 assigns "ship orders dropped when a Navarch is removed" to the future Ships / Navarchs page, and this leaf's own brief lists "ship order rules (Ships)" under Does NOT own. The sentence is exactly one sentence about another page's topic, so it doesn't cross the must_fix bar, but a reader who just read "orders stay and keep building" has to backtrack to reconcile it with ships apparently NOT continuing, with no transition explaining the split.
clarity_findings.fix: Either drop the sentence (it isn't in the brief) or add a one-clause transition that flags the exception explicitly, e.g. "...you can no longer cancel those orders. Ship orders are the exception: your Navarchs' ship orders there are cancelled instead, with no refund."

clarity_findings.problem: Line 46: "A tile takes one order at a time. While it is being built, upgraded or repaired, it takes no other order until that one finishes or is cancelled." The first sentence ("one order at a time") is fully subsumed by the second ("takes no other order until..."), so the first reads as a redundant lead-in rather than adding new information.
clarity_findings.fix: Merge into one sentence, e.g. "A tile being built, upgraded or repaired takes no other order until that one finishes or is cancelled."
